name.value: Sidney Spit Campsite / BC Marine Trail

description.value: A celebrated sandy spit on Sidney Island in the Gulf Islands, reached only by seasonal passenger ferry or private boat from Sidney; the beach and warm shallow water are the draw, but the water-only access makes it a non-starter for a loaded bike without advance planning.

address.value: Southern Gulf Islands, BC V0N 2Y0, Canada

raw_osm.access:description: Site closed for hunting 1 Nov - 28 Feb. IMPORTANT 100% reservable from May 15 to Sept 30 so paddlers advised to reserve. 2 small overflow areas. Mid-week sites often available on first first served basis. 250-654-4000,Toll-free: 1-866-944-1744
raw_osm.description: Open grassy sites, tent pads. Picnic tables. Gear carts. Picnic shelter. Vault toilets. Fee charged May - Sept.
raw_osm.description:approach: Easy sheltered sand beach at all water levels. BW aspect. Small seasonal dock. W aspect. Lagoon closed to all boating.
raw_osm.description:other: Site no longer offers drinking water. Trails. Swimming. Anchorage. Birding, fallow deer, wildlife. Frequent foot passenger ferry in summer from Sidney. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.
raw_osm.name: Sidney Spit Campsite / BC Marine Trail

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The specific BC Marine Trails page for this campsite returned a 404 (content migrated to member map), so all amenity evidence comes from OSM tags. The access:description confirms reservations are accepted May 15–Sept 30. The site is on Sidney Island within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, accessible primarily by seasonal foot passenger ferry or boat, which is a material limitation for touring cyclists.

Site is on Sidney Island and is accessible primarily by water (seasonal foot passenger ferry or private boat); direct bicycle access is not possible, which may limit relevance for road-touring cyclists.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a real, publicly accessible campsite within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve with active reservations and OSM-confirmed facilities. The foot passenger ferry connection to Sidney makes it reachable without a private boat.
